title: Cellular Mitosis Division Process Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D cellular mitosis simulation using Three.js (CDN). The simulation models a eukaryotic cell undergoing the major phases of mitotic division: Interphase, Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase, and Cytokinesis.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark navy background (0x0a0a2e). PerspectiveCamera at (0, 0, 18), lookAt origin.
- AmbientLight (0x334466, 0.4) and two PointLights: one warm (0xffeedd) at (10,10,10) intensity 0.8, one cool (0x88aaff) at (-10,-5,8) intensity 0.5.
- OrbitControls enabled for camera rotation/zoom.

CELL MODEL:
- The parent cell is a semi-transparent sphere (radius 3, 0x44cc88, opacity 0.3) representing the cell membrane.
- Inside, a smaller opaque sphere (radius 1.2, 0x6644aa) represents the nucleus.
- 8 chromosome objects (small elongated capsule/cylinder shapes, 0xff4488) initially inside the nucleus, randomly positioned within nucleus radius.
- Two centriole markers (tiny 0xffaa00 spheres, radius 0.15) initially near the nucleus.
- A cleavage furrow ring (TorusGeometry, 0x00ffaa) that appears during Cytokinesis.

PHASE PROGRESSION & PHYSICS:
- The simulation progresses through 6 phases: INTERPHASE -> PROPHASE -> METAPHASE -> ANAPHASE -> TELOPHASE -> CYTOKINESIS.
- User advances phases by pressing SPACEBAR. User can rewind one phase by pressing 'Z' (undo). User can redo with 'Y'.
- INTERPHASE: Cell is at rest. Nucleus visible. Chromosomes loosely distributed inside nucleus. Centrioles near nucleus center.
- PROPHASE: Nucleus membrane starts dissolving (opacity fades to 0.05 over transition). Chromosomes condense and become visible (scale up by 1.5x). Centrioles migrate to opposite poles (y = +3.5 and y = -3.5).
- METAPHASE: Chromosomes align along the equatorial plate (y ≈ 0, spread in x/z within radius 1.5). Spindle fibers appear as thin lines from centrioles to each chromosome.
- ANAPHASE: Each chromosome splits into two sister chromatids. The 8 originals move toward +y pole, 8 duplicates move toward -y pole. Total chromosome count becomes 16. Conservation law: total chromatid count must equal 16 at all times after split.
- TELOPHASE: Two new nuclear membranes form around each chromosome cluster (two new nucleus spheres at y=+3 and y=-3). Chromosomes decondense (scale back to 1.0x). Spindle fibers disappear.
- CYTOKINESIS: Cleavage furrow ring appears at y=0 and contracts (scale from 1.0 to 0.1 on x/z). Cell membrane elongates along y-axis (scaleY to 1.8) then splits into two daughter cell meshes. Each daughter cell contains one nucleus and 8 chromatids.

UI / HUD:
- A top-left HUD panel (DOM overlay) showing: current phase name, chromosome count, a progress bar (0-100% within current phase).
- A 'Reset' button that returns everything to INTERPHASE.
- A 'Toggle Labels' button that shows/hides 3D text labels (CSS2D or sprite) on key structures.
- A speed slider (range 0.5x to 3.0x) controlling animation speed multiplier.
- A 'Play/Pause' toggle button: when Play is active, phases auto-advance every 5 seconds (adjusted by speed). When paused, only SPACEBAR advances.

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
Expose the following on every animation frame:
{
  phase: string,           // 'INTERPHASE'|'PROPHASE'|'METAPHASE'|'ANAPHASE'|'TELOPHASE'|'CYTOKINESIS'
  phaseIndex: number,      // 0-5
  chromosomeCount: number, // 8 initially, 16 after ANAPHASE split
  nucleusOpacity: number,  // 1.0 in INTERPHASE, ~0.05 after PROPHASE
  centriolePositions: [{x,y,z},{x,y,z}], // two centriole world positions
  chromosomeScaleFactor: number, // 1.0 normal, 1.5 condensed
  spindleFibersVisible: boolean,
  cleavageFurrowScale: number,  // 1.0 to 0.1 during cytokinesis
  cellMembraneScaleY: number,   // 1.0 normally, up to 1.8 during cytokinesis
  daughterCellCount: number,    // 0 before cytokinesis complete, 2 after
  isPlaying: boolean,
  speedMultiplier: number,
  labelsVisible: boolean,
  phaseProgress: number,   // 0.0 to 1.0 within current phase
  undoStack: number[],     // array of phaseIndex values for undo
  redoStack: number[],     // array of phaseIndex values for redo
  totalChromatids: number  // conservation check: always 16 after anaphase (8 pairs)
}

ANIMATION:
- Phase transitions should animate smoothly over ~2 seconds (divided by speedMultiplier).
- Chromosomes should have subtle floating motion (sine-based oscillation) when not actively transitioning.
- The cleavage furrow should pulse gently (emissive oscillation) before contracting.

CONSERVATION LAWS:
- Total genetic material is conserved: before ANAPHASE, 8 chromosomes; after ANAPHASE split, exactly 16 chromatids (8 per pole).
- After CYTOKINESIS, each daughter cell must contain exactly 8 chromatids and 1 nucleus.
- No position values should ever be NaN or Infinity.
physics_constraints: Chromosome count conservation: 8 pre-split, 16 post-split (ANAPHASE onward). Each daughter cell post-cytokinesis must have exactly 8 chromatids. Centriole separation must reach opposite poles (|y| >= 3.0) by METAPHASE. Cleavage furrow contracts monotonically during CYTOKINESIS. No NaN/Infinity in any position or scale values. Total chromatid count is invariant after ANAPHASE.
